## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Sekhiya 26 (*Pallatthika*, "Clasping the knees") is a training rule from the *Sekhiya* section of the Vinaya Piṭaka's Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga [SuttaCentral]. The rule addresses bodily decorum for monastic conduct in inhabited areas, specifically prohibiting sitting with one's knees clasped or "lolling" by supporting oneself with the hands or with strips of cloth wrapped around the legs and body [Horner; SuttaCentral]. An English translation of the rule and its associated case narrative is provided by Bhikkhu Brahmali [SuttaCentral].
In terms of text reuse, DharmaNexus identifies 100 matching passages across 46 other Pali texts, primarily consisting of the stock Vinaya phrasing shared with other rules in the *Sekhiya* class, such as Sekhiya 22, Sekhiya 65, Sekhiya 16, Sekhiya 18, and Sekhiya 25 [DharmaNexus]. Beyond the Theravāda tradition, SuttaCentral lists full parallels across the Bhikkhu and Bhikkhunī Pātimokkhas and Vibhaṅgas of virtually all major early Buddhist monastic lineages, including the Sarvāstivāda, Mūlasarvāstivāda, Mahīśāsaka, Mahāsāṅghika, and Lokottaravāda recensions preserved in Chinese and Sanskrit [SuttaCentral].
